title: The New Look of the Indoor Football Index
body:
A New Look for the Indoor Football Index

The Indoor Football Index just got a full overhaul. Every team, player, league, and game in the archive now has a real page — built from the same data you already track, not a static site that goes stale the moment a season ends.

What's new

  • Team pages

  • Franchise history, coaching timelines, logo history, franchise records, and a season-by-season breakdown for every team in the archive — active or long since folded.

  • Player pages

  • Career stats broken out by category — passing, rushing, receiving, defense, special teams — with a career total row that actually adds up correctly across every team a player has suited up for.

  • A real schedule

  • Search and filter thousands of games by team, league, year, or week — not just a handful of recent scores.

  • Scorigami

  • Every final score combination that's ever happened in indoor and arena football, going back to 1987.

Why it matters

This isn’t a rebuild for its own sake. The old site couldn’t keep up with how much data was actually being tracked behind the scenes — box scores, franchise records, league history. The new version is built so that updating a single spreadsheet updates the whole site at once.

More leagues, more seasons, and more history are still being added. This is just the foundation.

title: Four Teams Set to Join the IFL for 2027
body:
Four Teams Set to Join the IFL for 2027

The IFL is set to add four teams for the 2027 season — three brand-new expansion franchises and one club jumping over from another league.

The additions

Athens — an expansion franchise, with a team name still to be announced.

Savannah — also expanding into the IFL for 2027, with its team name likewise still to be announced.

Texas Draft — the league’s third new expansion team for 2027.

Arkansas Diamonds — not a new franchise, but a league jump: the Diamonds are moving over to the IFL from TAL for the 2027 season.

Still to come

  • Team names for the Athens and Savannah franchises

  • Divisional alignment for all four additions

  • Full 2027 schedule release

title: Arizona Wins It All in a Wild 2026 IFL Season
body:
Arizona Wins It All in a Wild 2026 IFL Season

The 2026 IFL season delivered one of the most competitive playoff races in years, and it ended with the Arizona Rattlers hoisting the championship after a 62–51 win over the Green Bay Blizzard on August 16.

The road to the title

Green Bay entered the postseason as the West’s hottest team, closing the regular season 13–3 — a franchise-best mark — before running through the playoff bracket. San Diego Strike Force matched that exact regular-season record at 13–3 and claimed the #1 seed in the West, but their run ended one round short, falling to Arizona in the West Championship.

Arizona carried that momentum all the way to the title game, where they outlasted Green Bay in a back-and-forth final to close out the season as IFL champions.

Season notes

  • Green Bay Blizzard finished 13–3, the best regular season in franchise history.

  • San Diego Strike Force matched Green Bay at 13–3 and earned the #1 seed in the West.

  • Arizona Rattlers capped the season 62–51 over Green Bay to win the IFL Championship.

Full box scores for every 2026 game are available on the Schedule page, and complete season-by-season breakdowns are on each team’s page.
